title: Install R

blocks.what_we_do:
Install R from [CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org/), the official website for R. Follow these actions:

1. Open the CRAN page. Click the link for your system: "Download R for Windows", "Download R for macOS" or "Download R for Linux".
2. On Windows, click "base" (or "install R for the first time"). Then click the link at the top that starts with "Download R" and ends with "for Windows".
3. On macOS, click the `.pkg` file for your processor. Use the `arm64` file for Apple Silicon. Use the `x86_64` file for an Intel Mac. File names on the page can change a little.
4. On Linux, follow the CRAN instructions for your distribution. Installing packages may need an administrator.
5. Open the downloaded file. Accept the default choices. Click "Next" on Windows or "Continue" on macOS until the installer ends. If the computer asks for permission or a password, give it.

After the installation you should see a new program called R. On Windows it is in the Start menu. On macOS it is in the Applications folder.
blocks.why: R reads the commands in the notebooks and runs them. An [R package](../docs/glossary.md#r-package) is an add-on that gives R more functions. Packages do not replace R itself.
blocks.you_need: The system and processor you found at step 0.1. On a Mac with Apple Silicon, use the ARM64 build. On an Intel Mac, use the Intel build. Do not mix the two.
blocks.command:
Open R from the Start menu or the Applications folder. A window with a `>` prompt appears. Type this command and press Enter:

```{r s0-2_r_version}
R.version.string
```

Terminal equivalent: `Rscript --version`. The option `--version` prints the installed version without running an analysis. If the terminal cannot find `Rscript` but RStudio can run R, use the R console. You do not need to set up the terminal's PATH (the list of folders where it looks for programs) here.
blocks.expected_result: R prints one line that begins `R version`. Your version may differ from the Windows validation environment, which used R 4.5.2. The author also tested Ubuntu extraction with R 4.6.1.
blocks.troubleshooting: If your computer blocks the installation, ask the instructor or your institution's support team for an approved installation. Do not change your system language.
